03-01.title: Frédéric Chopin
03-01.description: Polish Romantic composer whose exquisitely lyrical solo piano works — nocturnes, études, and mazurkas — forever defined the expressive possibilities of the instrument.

03-01.title: Harry Belafonte
03-01.description: Jamaican-American singer and activist who brought calypso music to the world with 'Banana Boat Song' and used his fame as a platform for the civil rights movement.

03-01.title: Ron Howard
03-01.description: Child actor from The Andy Griffith Show who grew into one of Hollywood's most acclaimed directors, winning the Best Director Oscar for A Beautiful Mind.

03-01.title: Yellowstone National Park Established
03-01.description: President Ulysses S. Grant signed the act creating Yellowstone, the world's first national park, protecting 2.2 million acres of geothermal wilderness in Wyoming.

03-01.title: Zimmermann Telegram Published
03-01.description: American newspapers reprinted Germany's secret telegram proposing a military alliance with Mexico, outaging the public and pushing the US toward entering World War I.

03-01.title: "Dark Side of the Moon" — Pink Floyd
03-01.description: Pink Floyd's meditation on time, madness, and mortality was released on this day, spending a record-shattering 937 weeks on the Billboard 200.

03-01.title: Dune: Part Two
03-01.description: Denis Villeneuve's breathtaking second chapter of Frank Herbert's sci-fi epic sent Paul Atreides into the desert with the Fremen — and into global box-office history.

03-02.title: Dr. Seuss
03-02.description: American children's author and illustrator whose whimsical rhyming stories — The Cat in the Hat, Green Eggs and Ham — taught generations to love reading.

03-02.title: Jon Bon Jovi
03-02.description: New Jersey rocker who fronted one of the best-selling bands of the 1980s, with anthems like 'Livin' on a Prayer' cementing him as an arena rock icon.

03-02.title: Daniel Craig
03-02.description: British actor who reinvented James Bond for a grittier era in Casino Royale, bringing raw vulnerability to the secret agent role across five films.

03-02.title: Slave Import Ban Signed
03-02.description: The U.S. Congress passed an act prohibiting the importation of enslaved people, a landmark step that took effect January 1, 1808.

03-02.title: Wilt Chamberlain Scores 100 Points
03-02.description: Philadelphia Warriors center Wilt Chamberlain made NBA history by scoring an unbroken record of 100 points against the New York Knicks in Hershey, Pennsylvania.

03-02.title: "I'm a Man" — Bo Diddley
03-02.description: Bo Diddley recorded this electrifying blues stomp, built on his signature syncopated 'Bo Diddley beat' that would influence rock and roll for decades.

03-02.title: Real Madrid C.F. Founded
03-02.description: Spain's most storied football club was founded in Madrid, going on to win a record number of UEFA Champions League titles and become a global sporting institution.

03-03.title: Alexander Graham Bell
03-03.description: Scottish-American inventor whose first telephone call in 1876 — 'Mr. Watson, come here' — launched the age of instant voice communication.

03-03.title: Jean Harlow
03-03.description: Platinum-blonde Hollywood actress dubbed the 'Blonde Bombshell,' whose comedic timing and magnetic screen presence made her a defining star of the 1930s.

03-03.title: Camila Cabello
03-03.description: Cuban-American singer who rose to fame with Fifth Harmony before launching a solo career with the global hit 'Havana,' a love letter to her homeland.

03-03.title: Star-Spangled Banner Becomes National Anthem
03-03.description: Congress officially adopted Francis Scott Key's poem set to music as the national anthem of the United States, over a century after it was written during the War of 1812.

03-03.title: Time Magazine First Published
03-03.description: Henry Luce and Briton Hadden launched Time, the first weekly news magazine in the United States, transforming how Americans consumed news and coining 'Man of the Year.'

03-03.title: "Master of Puppets" — Metallica
03-03.description: Metallica's third album, widely regarded as the greatest heavy metal record ever made, showcased the band's unmatched technical ferocity and compositional ambition.

03-03.title: Carmen (Opera Premiere)
03-03.description: Bizet's scandalous opera about a fiery Romani woman premiered at the Opéra-Comique in Paris to a shocked audience — it later became one of the most performed operas in history.

03-04.title: Antonio Vivaldi
03-04.description: Venetian Baroque composer whose Four Seasons concertos blazed with dramatic color and virtuosity, making him one of the most celebrated musicians of his era.

03-04.title: Garrett Morgan
03-04.description: African-American inventor who patented the three-position traffic signal and the gas mask, both of which saved countless lives and transformed public safety.

03-04.title: Knute Rockne
03-04.description: Notre Dame football coach whose innovative strategies and inspirational leadership produced a .881 winning percentage — the best in college football history.

03-04.title: FDR's First Inauguration
03-04.description: Franklin D. Roosevelt took the oath of office and delivered his famous 'nothing to fear but fear itself' address as America languished in the depths of the Great Depression.

03-04.title: Chicago Incorporated as a City
03-04.description: The city of Chicago was officially incorporated with a population of about 4,200 — within decades it would grow into one of the world's great industrial metropolises.

03-04.title: "Closing Time" — Tom Waits
03-04.description: Tom Waits's debut album of smoky, late-night piano ballads and barroom poetry introduced one of rock's most original voices to a world that wasn't quite ready.

03-04.title: Grease
03-04.description: The musical phenomenon starring John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John became the highest-grossing movie musical of its era, with a soundtrack that defined a generation.

03-05.title: John Frusciante
03-05.description: Red Hot Chili Peppers guitarist whose melodic, emotionally charged playing on albums like Blood Sugar Sex Magik cemented him as one of rock's most beloved guitarists.

03-05.title: Rosa Luxemburg
03-05.description: German-Polish socialist philosopher and revolutionary whose passionate writings on democracy and imperialism made her a towering, martyred figure of the left.

03-05.title: Heitor Villa-Lobos
03-05.description: Brazilian composer who fused indigenous Amazonian melodies with European classical structures, producing some of the most distinctly national music of the 20th century.

03-05.title: Boston Massacre
03-05.description: British soldiers fired into a crowd of colonists on King Street, killing five including Crispus Attucks, inflaming anti-British sentiment that would ignite the Revolution.

03-05.title: Winston Churchill's Iron Curtain Speech
03-05.description: Churchill warned the world at Westminster College, Missouri that an 'iron curtain' had descended across Europe, effectively naming the Cold War before it had a name.

03-05.title: "For Your Love" — The Yardbirds
03-05.description: The Yardbirds released this harpsichord-driven single, a commercial smash that pushed Eric Clapton out and ushered in Jeff Beck, reshaping British rock's trajectory.

03-05.title: Ben-Hur
03-05.description: William Wyler's Roman epic starring Charlton Heston won a then-record eleven Academy Awards, including Best Picture, setting the standard for Hollywood spectacle.

03-06.title: Michelangelo
03-06.description: Renaissance genius whose Sistine Chapel ceiling and statue of David stand as the supreme achievements of Western art, sculpted and painted with almost supernatural skill.

03-06.title: David Gilmour
03-06.description: Pink Floyd's guitarist and co-vocalist, whose spacious, singing tone and emotionally devastating solos defined the sound of progressive rock's most poetic band.

03-06.title: Shaquille O'Neal
03-06.description: Dominant NBA center who won four championships with two franchises, combining an unstoppable seven-foot frame with unexpected charisma and media star power.

03-06.title: Ghana Independence
03-06.description: Ghana became the first Sub-Saharan African nation to gain independence from British colonial rule, with Kwame Nkrumah declaring a new era for the continent.

03-06.title: Muhammad Ali Gets His Name
03-06.description: Nation of Islam leader Elijah Muhammad officially gave boxing champion Cassius Clay the name Muhammad Ali, days after his stunning upset of Sonny Liston.

03-06.title: "Can't Buy Me Love" — The Beatles
03-06.description: The Beatles' Paul McCartney penned this joyous rocker, which sold two million copies in its opening week and became the first hit they recorded outside of Britain.

03-06.title: The Last Emperor
03-06.description: Bernardo Bertolucci's sweeping epic about China's final dynastic ruler won all nine Academy Awards for which it was nominated, including Best Picture and Best Director.

03-07.title: Maurice Ravel
03-07.description: French impressionist composer whose orchestral showpiece Boléro — a single melody repeated with rising orchestration — became one of the most performed pieces in classical music.

03-07.title: Townes Van Zandt
03-07.description: Texas troubadour whose devastating folk songs like 'Pancho and Lefty' and 'If I Needed You' are considered the finest in American country music by those who truly know.

03-07.title: Bryan Cranston
03-07.description: Emmy-winning actor whose transformation from sitcom dad on Malcolm in the Middle to meth kingpin Walter White on Breaking Bad is television acting's greatest career arc.

03-07.title: Bloody Sunday in Selma
03-07.description: State troopers attacked peaceful civil rights marchers on the Edmund Pettus Bridge, broadcasting brutal images that galvanized the nation and led directly to the Voting Rights Act.

03-07.title: Alexander Graham Bell Patents the Telephone
03-07.description: The U.S. Patent Office granted Alexander Graham Bell Patent No. 174,465 for 'the method of, and apparatus for, transmitting vocal or other sounds telegraphically.'

03-07.title: "Licensed to Ill" — Beastie Boys
03-07.description: Beastie Boys became the first hip-hop act to have a number-one album in the US, with their raucous debut earning Diamond certification and a permanent place in rap history.

03-07.title: The Hurt Locker
03-07.description: Kathryn Bigelow made Academy Awards history when she became the first woman to win Best Director for this visceral Iraq War thriller at the 82nd ceremony.

03-08.title: Micky Dolenz
03-08.description: Drummer and lead vocalist of The Monkees whose exuberant performances on 'I'm a Believer' and 'Daydream Believer' made him the face of America's favorite manufactured pop band.

03-08.title: Gary Numan
03-08.description: British synth-pop pioneer whose robotic 'Cars' and 'Are Friends Electric?' defined the cold, machine-driven sound of the early electronic music era.

03-08.title: Cyd Charisse
03-08.description: MGM's most electrifying dancer whose impossibly long legs and classical ballet training lit up Singin' in the Rain and The Band Wagon in unforgettable sequences.

03-08.title: International Women's Day
03-08.description: Women in Petrograd marched for bread and peace on this day, sparking the February Revolution that would topple the Tsar — the anniversary became International Women's Day.

03-08.title: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 Disappears
03-08.description: A Boeing 777 carrying 239 people vanished from radar en route from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing, becoming the greatest aviation mystery of the modern era.

03-08.title: "I Want You" — Marvin Gaye
03-08.description: Marvin Gaye's lush, sensual album reached No. 1 on the R&B chart, featuring Leon Ware's production that made it one of the most deeply felt romantic records ever made.

03-08.title: Moonlight
03-08.description: Barry Jenkins's tender portrait of a Black gay man's coming-of-age in Miami won the Best Picture Oscar at the most dramatic ceremony in Academy Awards history.

03-09.title: Oscar Isaac
03-09.description: Guatemalan-American actor whose chameleonic range — from the tormented musician of Inside Llewyn Davis to Poe Dameron in Star Wars — made him one of his generation's finest.

03-09.title: Bobby Fischer
03-09.description: Brooklyn-born chess prodigy who became world champion in 1972 with a Cold War match against Boris Spassky that transfixed the entire globe.

03-09.title: Juliette Binoche
03-09.description: French actress whose Oscar-winning performance in The English Patient and roles in Chocolat and Certified Copy established her as European cinema's most luminous star.

03-09.title: Battle of the Ironclads
03-09.description: The USS Monitor and CSS Virginia fought to a historic draw at Hampton Roads — the first battle between iron-armored warships that made wooden navies obsolete overnight.

03-09.title: The Notorious B.I.G. Killed
03-09.description: Brooklyn rapper Biggie Smalls was shot dead at a Los Angeles stoplight, bringing the East Coast–West Coast hip-hop feud to its tragic, unresolved conclusion.

03-09.title: "The Wealth of Nations" Published — Adam Smith
03-09.description: Adam Smith published his foundational text of modern economics, arguing that free markets and the 'invisible hand' create wealth more efficiently than government control.

03-09.title: The Addams Family
03-09.description: Barry Sonnenfeld's pitch-black comedy brought the macabre cartoon family to life with Raul Julia's magnetic Gomez and Anjelica Huston's imperious Morticia.

03-10.title: Harriet Tubman
03-10.description: Conductor of the Underground Railroad who freed herself from slavery and returned south at least thirteen times to liberate around 70 others, never losing a passenger.

03-10.title: Carrie Underwood
03-10.description: Oklahoma-born country superstar whose American Idol victory launched a career that produced 'Before He Cheats,' 'Jesus, Take the Wheel,' and eight Grammy Awards.

03-10.title: Jon Hamm
03-10.description: American actor whose brooding, perfectly-suited portrayal of ad man Don Draper in Mad Men brought Emmy gold and redefined the antihero for prestige television.

03-10.title: First Telephone Call
03-10.description: Alexander Graham Bell made the first successful telephone call — 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you' — from one room to another in his Boston laboratory.

03-10.title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo Ratified
03-10.description: The U.S. Senate ratified the treaty ending the Mexican-American War, with Mexico ceding 525,000 square miles including California, New Mexico, and Arizona.

03-10.title: "The Joshua Tree" — U2
03-10.description: U2's monumental fifth album, with its trio of aching anthems about America, debuted at number one in the UK and turned Bono's band into the biggest rock act on the planet.

03-10.title: Chinatown
03-10.description: Roman Polanski's neo-noir masterpiece starring Jack Nicholson as a private detective ensnared in Los Angeles's dark water wars remains the gold standard of American crime cinema.

03-11.title: Bobby McFerrin
03-11.description: Virtuoso vocalist and conductor who stunned the world with 'Don't Worry, Be Happy,' the first a cappella song to reach number one on the Billboard Hot 100.

03-11.title: Douglas Adams
03-11.description: British author who turned absurdist comedy into cosmic philosophy with The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, in which the answer to life, the universe, and everything is 42.

03-11.title: Rupert Murdoch
03-11.description: Australian-American media mogul who built a global empire across newspapers, film studios, and television networks, reshaping politics and popular culture for decades.

03-11.title: Madrid Train Bombings
03-11.description: Ten bombs on four commuter trains killed 193 people and wounded nearly 2,000 in Spain's deadliest terrorist attack, carried out by an al-Qaeda-linked cell.

03-11.title: A Raisin in the Sun Opens on Broadway
03-11.description: Lorraine Hansberry became the first Black woman to have a play on Broadway with this groundbreaking drama about a Black family's dreams deferred in Chicago.

03-11.title: "Bat Out of Hell" — Meat Loaf
03-11.description: Meat Loaf's operatic rock debut began its astonishing 416-week run on the UK charts, making it one of the best-selling albums in history at over 43 million copies.

03-11.title: The Conversation
03-11.description: Francis Ford Coppola's paranoid surveillance thriller starring Gene Hackman as a guilt-ridden wiretapper won the Palme d'Or at Cannes and predicted the surveillance age.

03-12.title: Jack Kerouac
03-12.description: Beat Generation novelist whose spontaneous prose masterpiece On the Road captured a restless America in the early 1950s and became the bible of youth rebellion.

03-12.title: Liza Minnelli
03-12.description: Tony, Oscar, Emmy, and Grammy-winning entertainer whose electrifying Cabaret performance showed the world she was far more than just Judy Garland's daughter.

03-12.title: James Taylor
03-12.description: Soft-rock singer-songwriter whose gentle 'Fire and Rain' and 'You've Got a Friend' defined the introspective, acoustic sound of the early 1970s.

03-12.title: World Wide Web Proposal
03-12.description: Tim Berners-Lee submitted his proposal for an information management system at CERN — the document that would become the blueprint for the World Wide Web.

03-12.title: Pope Francis Elected
03-12.description: Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio of Argentina was elected as the 266th Pope, becoming the first Latin American pontiff and taking the humble name Francis.

03-12.title: "It's Not Unusual" — Tom Jones
03-12.description: Tom Jones reached number one in the UK with his powerhouse debut, a brassy pop gem that launched the Welsh belter onto the world stage at just twenty-four years old.

03-12.title: The Godfather Part II
03-12.description: Coppola's audacious sequel — one of the few films to surpass its predecessor — became the first sequel to win the Academy Award for Best Picture.

03-13.title: William H. Macy
03-13.description: Character actor of uncommon depth whose bumbling, desperate Jerry Lundegaard in Fargo earned him an Oscar nomination and secured his status as a Hollywood legend.

03-13.title: Emile Hirsch
03-13.description: Actor who delivered one of the most committed performances of his generation as doomed wilderness wanderer Chris McCandless in Sean Penn's Into the Wild.

03-13.title: Mikaela Shiffrin
03-13.description: American alpine skier who shattered every world record for World Cup wins, combining technical perfection with fierce competitive will to become skiing's GOAT.

03-13.title: Uranus Discovered
03-13.description: William Herschel spotted an unfamiliar object through his telescope in Bath, England — the first planet ever discovered with a telescope, instantly doubling the solar system.

03-13.title: Pope Francis Elected
03-13.description: White smoke rose from the Sistine Chapel as Cardinal Bergoglio of Buenos Aires emerged as Pope Francis, the first Jesuit and first South American to lead the Catholic Church.

03-13.title: "Ray of Light" — Madonna
03-13.description: Madonna's electronica-inflected album debuted at number one in the UK and earned four Grammy Awards, marking her most critically acclaimed artistic reinvention.
Sam Mendes's bravura WWI film, shot to appear as a single unbroken take, followed two soldiers racing through No Man's Land on a desperate mission to prevent a massacre.

03-14.title: Albert Einstein
03-14.description: German-born physicist whose special and general theories of relativity and famous equation E=mc² fundamentally reshaped our understanding of space, time, and the universe.

03-14.title: Quincy Jones
03-14.description: Legendary producer and arranger who helmed Michael Jackson's Thriller — the best-selling album of all time — and transformed pop music with his orchestral ambition.

03-14.title: Billy Crystal
03-14.description: Comedian and filmmaker beloved for When Harry Met Sally and City Slickers who charmed millions as the nine-time host of the Academy Awards.

03-14.title: Eli Whitney Patents the Cotton Gin
03-14.description: Eli Whitney's device for mechanically separating cotton fiber from its seeds vastly expanded the plantation economy — and tragically deepened the institution of slavery.

03-14.title: Xi Jinping Elected President of China
03-14.description: Xi Jinping was formally elected President of the People's Republic of China, beginning a tenure that would concentrate more power in one leader than any since Mao Zedong.

03-14.title: "Thriller" — Michael Jackson
03-14.description: Michael Jackson's Thriller album won a record eight Grammy Awards at the 1984 ceremony, cementing it as the greatest-selling album in music history.

03-14.title: The Color Purple
03-14.description: Steven Spielberg's emotional adaptation of Alice Walker's novel earned eleven Oscar nominations and introduced Whoopi Goldberg and Oprah Winfrey to film audiences.

03-15.title: Sly Stone
03-15.description: Visionary bandleader of Sly and the Family Stone whose integrated funk group pioneered the psychedelic soul sound that influenced everything from hip-hop to disco.

03-15.title: Mike Love
03-15.description: Co-founder and lead vocalist of The Beach Boys whose honey-sweet tenor anchored the California sound on anthems like 'Surfin' U.S.A.' and 'Good Vibrations.'

03-15.title: Eva Longoria
03-15.description: Texas-born actress who became a global star as the glamorous Gabrielle Solis on Desperate Housewives, later channeling her celebrity into Latino rights advocacy.

03-15.title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
03-15.description: On the Ides of March, Roman dictator Julius Caesar was stabbed 23 times on the Senate floor by 60 conspirators including Brutus — the event that ended the Roman Republic.

03-15.title: My Fair Lady Opens on Broadway
03-15.description: Lerner and Loewe's musical adaptation of Pygmalion opened at the Mark Hellinger Theatre and ran for 2,717 performances, then a Broadway record.

03-15.title: "Killing Me Softly with His Song" — Roberta Flack
03-15.description: Roberta Flack's hushed, devastating ballad began a five-week run at the top of the Billboard Hot 100, winning the Grammy for Record of the Year.

03-15.title: The Godfather
03-15.description: Francis Ford Coppola's Godfather premiered on this date — the film that defined American cinema in the 1970s won three Oscars and remains the greatest gangster film ever made.

03-16.title: James Madison
03-16.description: America's fourth president, the 'Father of the Constitution,' whose meticulous work at the Constitutional Convention and authorship of the Federalist Papers shaped American democracy.

03-16.title: Jerry Lewis
03-16.description: American comedian, actor, and filmmaker whose manic physical comedy made him a global star and — bizarrely — a high art icon worshipped by French intellectuals.

03-16.title: Flavor Flav
03-16.description: Public Enemy's hype man, clock-wearing showman, and unexpectedly brilliant vocalist whose manic energy gave hip-hop's most politically charged group its essential counterweight.

03-16.title: Robert Goddard Launches First Liquid-Fueled Rocket
03-16.description: Robert Goddard launched the world's first liquid-fueled rocket from his aunt's farm in Auburn, Massachusetts — a 2.5-second flight that opened the Space Age.

03-16.title: Battle of Iwo Jima Ends
03-16.description: After 36 days of ferocious combat, U.S. Marines declared Iwo Jima secured — the battle that produced the most famous war photograph in American history.

03-16.title: "Can't Buy Me Love" — The Beatles
03-16.description: Released worldwide, Can't Buy Me Love sold over a million advance copies in the United States alone, becoming the first pop single to achieve such pre-release numbers.

03-16.title: The Last Tango in Paris
03-16.description: Bernardo Bertolucci's controversial psychosexual drama with Marlon Brando scandalized audiences worldwide and became one of the most discussed art films of its era.

03-17.title: Nat King Cole
03-17.description: Jazz pianist who became one of the silkiest pop vocalists in history, with 'Unforgettable' and 'The Christmas Song' cementing a legacy of incomparable warmth.

03-17.title: Kurt Russell
03-17.description: Versatile Hollywood leading man whose performances for John Carpenter in The Thing and Escape from New York made him the ultimate grindhouse action hero.

03-17.title: Golda Meir
03-17.description: Iron-willed Ukrainian-born Israeli stateswoman who became Israel's first female Prime Minister in 1969, leading the country through the traumatic Yom Kippur War.

03-17.title: British Evacuation of Boston
03-17.description: After Washington and Knox positioned artillery on Dorchester Heights, the British army evacuated Boston, the first major American victory of the Revolutionary War.

03-17.title: First Solar-Powered Satellite Launched
03-17.description: The U.S. launched Vanguard 1, the first satellite powered by solar energy, which remains the oldest man-made object still in orbit around Earth.

03-17.title: "Janis Joplin's Me and Bobby McGee" — #1 Hit
03-17.description: Janis Joplin's raw recording of Kris Kristofferson's road song reached number one six months after her death, a posthumous chart-topper that broke the hearts of a generation.

03-17.title: Forrest Gump
03-17.description: Robert Zemeckis's endlessly quotable fable of an Alabama simpleton accidentally present at every major American cultural moment won six Oscars including Best Picture.

03-18.title: Wilson Pickett
03-18.description: Southern soul screamer whose electrifying 'In the Midnight Hour' and 'Mustang Sally' made him one of the greatest and most imitated voices of the 1960s.

03-18.title: Charley Pride
03-18.description: Country music legend who broke racial barriers as one of the first Black artists signed to RCA's Nashville roster, scoring 29 number-one country hits.

03-18.title: Queen Latifah
03-18.description: Pioneering rapper, actress, and producer who became the first hip-hop artist nominated for an acting Oscar for her role in Chicago, embodying hip-hop royalty.

03-18.title: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum Heist
03-18.description: Thieves disguised as police officers stole 13 works including a Vermeer and three Rembrandts from Boston's Gardner Museum in the largest art theft in history.

03-18.title: Tri-State Tornado
03-18.description: The deadliest tornado in U.S. history tore a 219-mile path through Missouri, Illinois, and Indiana, killing 695 people and leaving entire towns in ruin.

03-18.title: "Alexander's Ragtime Band" — Irving Berlin
03-18.description: Irving Berlin copyrighted this syncopated smash, the song that introduced ragtime to mainstream America and launched the modern era of popular music.

03-18.title: Chicago
03-18.description: Rob Marshall's flashy, razzle-dazzle musical revival won six Oscars including Best Picture and proved Hollywood could still make old-fashioned show-stopping spectacle.

03-19.title: Wyatt Earp
03-19.description: Frontier lawman whose role in the legendary Gunfight at the O.K. Corral in Tombstone, Arizona made him the defining figure of the Wild West mythology.

03-19.title: Bruce Willis
03-19.description: American action movie star whose wisecracking everyman John McClane in Die Hard redefined the 1980s action hero and spawned a franchise.

03-19.title: Glenn Close
03-19.description: Six-time Oscar-nominated actress whose unforgettable turn as the obsessive Alex Forrest in Fatal Attraction remains one of cinema's most iconic villains.

03-19.title: Sagrada Família Cornerstone Laid
03-19.description: The bishop of Barcelona laid the cornerstone of Antoni Gaudí's extraordinary basilica, beginning a construction project that the architect knew would outlast his own life.

03-19.title: Iraq War Begins
03-19.description: U.S. President George W. Bush ordered air strikes on Baghdad, launching the invasion of Iraq in a war that would last nearly a decade and reshape the Middle East.

03-19.title: "I've Got a Woman" — Ray Charles
03-19.description: Ray Charles topped the R&B charts with this roaring gospel-blues fusion that introduced his signature sound — secular joy sung with the fervor of a revival meeting.

03-19.title: Die Hard
03-19.description: John McTiernan's masterclass in action filmmaking introduced Bruce Willis's John McClane — an ordinary cop in extraordinary danger — and set the template for action cinema.

03-20.title: Fred Rogers
03-20.description: Gentle television minister who created Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, telling millions of children they were special exactly as they were — and meaning every single word.

03-20.title: Spike Lee
03-20.description: Brooklyn filmmaker whose Do the Right Thing, Malcolm X, and 25th Hour established him as American cinema's most vital and incendiary voice on race and urban life.

03-20.title: Holly Hunter
03-20.description: Academy Award-winning actress whose silent piano-playing Jane Campion protagonist in The Piano showed that screen presence needs no words.

03-20.title: John Lennon Marries Yoko Ono
03-20.description: John Lennon and Yoko Ono married in Gibraltar, then began their famous week-long 'Bed-In for Peace' in Amsterdam to protest the Vietnam War.

03-20.title: Tokyo Subway Sarin Attack
03-20.description: Members of the Aum Shinrikyo cult released sarin nerve gas on five Tokyo subway lines during morning rush hour, killing 13 and injuring thousands.

03-20.title: "After Hours" — The Weeknd
03-20.description: The Weeknd's brooding, neon-soaked masterpiece debuted at number one globally, with 'Blinding Lights' becoming one of the most-streamed songs in Spotify history.

03-20.title: The Piano
03-20.description: Jane Campion's haunting period drama won the Palme d'Or at Cannes and three Oscars — Holly Hunter's wordless performance as a mute Scottish pianist remains unforgettable.

03-21.title: Johann Sebastian Bach
03-21.description: German Baroque composer whose Brandenburg Concertos, St. Matthew Passion, and Well-Tempered Clavier represent the absolute summit of Western classical music.

03-21.title: Gary Oldman
03-21.description: British chameleon actor who played Dracula, Commissioner Gordon, Churchill, and Beethoven with equal conviction, winning his Oscar for Darkest Hour.

03-21.title: Matthew Broderick
03-21.description: American actor who embodied carefree youth as the charming, scheming Ferris Bueller in one of John Hughes's most beloved comedies.

03-21.title: Sharpeville Massacre
03-21.description: South African police opened fire on peaceful anti-apartheid protesters in Sharpeville, killing 69 people — the date became International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination.

03-21.title: Namibia Gains Independence
03-21.description: Namibia became Africa's last colony to gain independence after 75 years of South African rule, with Sam Nujoma sworn in as the nation's first president.

03-21.title: "The Joshua Tree" — U2
03-21.description: U2's chart-topping album entered the UK charts on this week, beginning a 156-week run that made it one of the defining documents of 1980s rock.

03-21.title: Ferris Bueller's Day Off
03-21.description: John Hughes's hymn to teenage liberation starring Matthew Broderick as the ultimate slacker hero captured the spirit of American adolescence so perfectly it never aged.

03-22.title: Andrew Lloyd Webber
03-22.description: The most successful Broadway and West End composer in history, whose Phantom of the Opera, Cats, and Evita redefined the possibilities of the modern musical.

03-22.title: Reese Witherspoon
03-22.description: Oscar-winning actress and producer whose breezy Elle Woods in Legally Blonde and fierce Cheryl Strayed in Wild showed the extraordinary range beneath her Southern charm.

03-22.title: William Shatner
03-22.description: Canadian actor who immortalized Captain James T. Kirk in Star Trek and later became the oldest human to travel to space, at age 90, on a Blue Origin flight.

03-22.title: British Stamp Act Passed
03-22.description: The British Parliament passed the Stamp Act imposing direct taxes on American colonies — the colonists' furious 'no taxation without representation' protests sparked the Revolution.

03-22.title: Lumière Brothers Demonstrate Film
03-22.description: Auguste and Louis Lumière publicly demonstrated their Cinématographe film technology in Paris — one of the pivotal moments in the birth of cinema.

03-22.title: "Far Beyond Driven" — Pantera
03-22.description: Pantera released one of the few extreme metal albums to debut at number one in America, a sonic bulldozer that proved heavy music could conquer the mainstream.

03-22.title: Legally Blonde
03-22.description: Reese Witherspoon's buoyant star-making performance as Elle Woods — proving that pink and smart are not mutually exclusive — became an enduring pop culture touchstone.

03-23.title: Joan Crawford
03-23.description: Golden Age Hollywood actress whose ferocious determination took her from chorus girl to Oscar winner for Mildred Pierce, surviving scandal and tabloid infamy.

03-23.title: Chaka Khan
03-23.description: Soul and funk powerhouse dubbed the 'Queen of Funk' whose searing voice led Rufus and launched a solo career that produced the jubilant anthem 'I'm Every Woman.'

03-23.title: Peter Lorre
03-23.description: Hungarian-American character actor whose distinctive voice and unsettling eyes made him unforgettable in Fritz Lang's M, The Maltese Falcon, and Casablanca.

03-23.title: Ever Given Blocks the Suez Canal
03-23.description: The massive container ship Ever Given ran aground in the Suez Canal, blocking global maritime trade for six days in a crisis watched by the entire internet.

03-23.title: Patrick Henry's 'Give Me Liberty' Speech
03-23.description: Firebrand patriot Patrick Henry electrified Virginia's Second Convention with his 'give me liberty, or give me death!' speech, rallying the colonies toward revolution.

03-23.title: "Elvis Presley" — Elvis Presley
03-23.description: Elvis's self-titled debut album was released on this date, spent ten weeks at number one, and became the first rock and roll record to top the album charts.

03-23.title: Titanic
03-23.description: James Cameron's ocean epic swept the 70th Academy Awards with 11 Oscars on this date, tying Ben-Hur's long-standing record and cementing its place in cinematic history.

03-24.title: Steve McQueen
03-24.description: The 'King of Cool' — actor whose simmering intensity in Bullitt, The Great Escape, and Papillon made him the defining masculine screen idol of the 1960s and 70s.

03-24.title: Jim Parsons
03-24.description: Texas-born actor who brought the brilliantly insufferable Sheldon Cooper to life on The Big Bang Theory for twelve seasons, winning four Emmy Awards.

03-24.title: Alyson Hannigan
03-24.description: Actress beloved for her sweetly powerful Willow Rosenberg in Buffy the Vampire Slayer and her comic timing as Lily Aldrin in How I Met Your Mother.

03-24.title: The Great Escape
03-24.description: Over 75 Allied POWs escaped through a tunnel from Stalag Luft III in Germany in a daring operation that inspired one of the most beloved war films ever made.

03-24.title: Exxon Valdez Oil Spill
03-24.description: The tanker Exxon Valdez ran aground in Prince William Sound, Alaska, spilling 11 million gallons of crude oil and devastating 1,300 miles of coastline.

03-24.title: "Wuthering Heights" — Kate Bush
03-24.description: Nineteen-year-old Kate Bush became the first woman to reach number one in the UK with a self-written song, her eerie falsetto telling Cathy's ghost story in three minutes.

03-24.title: The Great Escape
03-24.description: John Sturges's thrilling POW breakout epic starring Steve McQueen on his motorcycle became one of the most beloved and rewatched adventure films in cinema history.

03-25.title: Elton John
03-25.description: Flamboyant British rock legend who sold over 300 million records with hits like 'Rocket Man' and 'Tiny Dancer,' his sequined excess masking songwriting of profound depth.

03-25.title: Aretha Franklin
03-25.description: The Queen of Soul whose voice — deployed on 'Respect,' 'Chain of Fools,' and 'Natural Woman' — was not just the greatest in pop music but a force of moral authority.

03-25.title: Gloria Steinem
03-25.description: American feminist activist and journalist who co-founded Ms. Magazine and spent decades as the most recognizable and galvanizing voice of the women's liberation movement.

03-25.title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
03-25.description: A fire at a New York City garment factory killed 146 workers, mostly young immigrant women, prompting landmark labor laws and worker safety regulations.

03-25.title: Treaties of Rome Signed
03-25.description: Six European nations signed the Treaties of Rome, establishing the European Economic Community and laying the cornerstone for what would become the European Union.

03-25.title: "Respect" — Aretha Franklin
03-25.description: Aretha Franklin released her electrifying cover of Otis Redding's song, rewriting it as a feminist and civil rights anthem — R-E-S-P-E-C-T spelled out for eternity.

03-25.title: The Outsiders
03-25.description: Francis Ford Coppola's adaptation of S.E. Hinton's novel was a showcase for a spectacular young cast including Tom Cruise, Matt Dillon, and Rob Lowe.

03-26.title: Diana Ross
03-26.description: Lead singer of The Supremes, whose Motown hits made them the most successful American group of the 1960s before Ross launched a dazzling solo career.

03-26.title: Steven Tyler
03-26.description: Aerosmith's rubber-faced frontman whose elastic voice and absurd stage presence kept the Boston hard rock band rolling for five decades of arena-filling anthems.

03-26.title: Leonard Nimoy
03-26.description: American actor who gave the galaxy Mr. Spock — Star Trek's half-Vulcan science officer whose cold logic and suppressed emotions made him one of TV's most beloved characters.

03-26.title: Jonas Salk Announces Polio Vaccine
03-26.description: Dr. Jonas Salk announced the successful test of his polio vaccine, a breakthrough that would virtually eradicate a disease that had paralyzed millions of children.

03-26.title: Beethoven Dies
03-26.description: Ludwig van Beethoven died in Vienna at 56, deaf for the last decade of his life yet producing symphonies — including the Ninth — of staggering power and transcendence.

03-26.title: "MDNA" — Madonna
03-26.description: Madonna's twelfth studio album debuted at number one in America, giving her a record eighth chart-topping album and proving her pop dominance still undiminished.

03-26.title: The Matrix
03-26.description: The Wachowskis' mind-bending sci-fi thriller was released, introducing bullet-time photography and asking audiences if they'd take the red pill or the blue pill.

03-27.title: Quentin Tarantino
03-27.description: Maverick filmmaker whose Pulp Fiction, Reservoir Dogs, and Inglourious Basterds remixed genre cinema into postmodern pop art, making movie-love a revolutionary act.

03-27.title: Mariah Carey
03-27.description: Pop diva with the most number-one singles by a solo artist in American history, whose whistle-register stratosphere and emotional vulnerability made her the voice of a generation.

03-27.title: Mstislav Rostropovich
03-27.description: One of the 20th century's supreme cellists, whose interpretations of Dvorak and Shostakovich became definitive recordings while his courage stood up to Soviet persecution.

03-27.title: Eric Clapton Marries Pattie Boyd
03-27.description: Eric Clapton finally married Pattie Boyd, formerly the wife of his best friend George Harrison — a love triangle that inspired both 'Layla' and Harrison's 'Something.'

03-27.title: Tenerife Airport Disaster
03-27.description: Two Boeing 747s collided on the runway at Los Rodeos Airport, killing 583 people — the deadliest accident in aviation history, caused by fog and radio miscommunication.

03-27.title: "Livin' la Vida Loca" — Ricky Martin
03-27.description: Ricky Martin's explosive Latin pop hit reached number one in 17 countries, launching the Latin pop crossover explosion and his reinvention as a global superstar.

03-27.title: Pulp Fiction
03-27.description: Quentin Tarantino's Palme d'Or winner premiered at Cannes — its interlocking crime vignettes and breathtaking dialogue made it the most influential American film of the 1990s.

03-28.title: Lady Gaga
03-28.description: New York pop provocateur who arrived in a meat dress and left as one of the most versatile entertainers alive, her 'A Star Is Born' performance silencing every doubter.

03-28.title: Reba McEntire
03-28.description: Oklahoma-born country queen who became one of the best-selling female artists in music history, with a TV career and Broadway debut that proved her range boundless.

03-28.title: Vince Vaughn
03-28.description: Rapid-fire improvisational comedian whose motormouth charm in Swingers, Wedding Crashers, and Dodgeball made him the defining comedy actor of the early 2000s.

03-28.title: Three Mile Island Nuclear Accident
03-28.description: A cooling system failure at Pennsylvania's Three Mile Island plant caused a partial nuclear meltdown — America's worst nuclear accident fundamentally changed energy policy.

03-28.title: Rocky Wins Best Picture
03-28.description: At the 49th Academy Awards, John G. Avildsen's underdog boxing story Rocky defeated All the President's Men and Network to win Best Picture, stunning Hollywood.

03-28.title: "Billie Jean" — Michael Jackson
03-28.description: Michael Jackson's paranoid funk masterpiece from Thriller sat atop the U.S. charts, accompanied by the music video that introduced the moonwalk to a stunned world.

03-28.title: The Birds
03-28.description: Alfred Hitchcock's slow-burning horror film released on this date pitted Tippi Hedren against thousands of attacking birds in a masterclass of dread without explanation.

03-29.title: John Tyler
03-29.description: The 10th President of the United States who became the first VP to ascend to the presidency following William Henry Harrison's death just 31 days into office.

03-29.title: Eric Idle
03-29.description: Monty Python's wittiest wordsmith who gave the world 'Always Look on the Bright Side of Life' — a cheerful song about crucifixion that became a genuine pop anthem.

03-29.title: Astrud Gilberto
03-29.description: Brazilian singer whose breathy, ingenuous voice on 'The Girl from Ipanema' brought bossa nova to the world and became one of the most recognizable sounds of the 1960s.

03-29.title: British North America Act
03-29.description: The British Parliament passed the British North America Act, uniting Canada, Nova Scotia, and New Brunswick into the Dominion of Canada — the nation's founding document.

03-29.title: The King and I Opens on Broadway
03-29.description: Rodgers and Hammerstein's magnificent musical about a Welsh governess at the Siamese court opened on Broadway, making Yul Brynner an instant star.

03-29.title: "The Girl from Ipanema" — João Gilberto & Astrud Gilberto
03-29.description: Astrud Gilberto's hushed, tentative English verse on this bossa nova gem made it one of the most recorded songs in history and a permanent symbol of Brazilian cool.

03-29.title: Schindler's List
03-29.description: Steven Spielberg's devastating Holocaust masterpiece swept the 66th Academy Awards in March, winning seven Oscars including Best Picture and Best Director.

03-30.title: Eric Clapton
03-30.description: Three-time Rock and Roll Hall of Famer who reinvented the electric guitar through Cream, Blind Faith, and Layla — his blues-drenched virtuosity earning the nickname 'God.'

03-30.title: Tracy Chapman
03-30.description: Folk-rock singer-songwriter whose debut album and its urgent anthem 'Fast Car' captured the bleakness of American poverty with devastating simplicity.

03-30.title: Vincent van Gogh
03-30.description: Dutch Post-Impressionist whose 900 paintings — Starry Night, Sunflowers, Bedroom in Arles — were produced with delirious intensity in just a decade before his death.

03-30.title: Dalai Lama Flees Tibet
03-30.description: Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, fled across the Himalayas to India after China's military crackdown on a Tibetan uprising, beginning six decades in exile.

03-30.title: Alaska Purchased from Russia
03-30.description: The United States purchased Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million — mocked as 'Seward's Folly' until gold was discovered and Alaska proved worth far more than the price.

03-30.title: "Fast Car" — Tracy Chapman
03-30.description: Tracy Chapman's quietly devastating folk-pop breakthrough gave voice to lives trapped by poverty with a simplicity that made it one of the most affecting debut singles ever.

03-30.title: Ordinary People
03-30.description: Robert Redford's directorial debut — a study of upper-middle-class grief with Timothy Hutton and Donald Sutherland — won Best Picture and Best Director at the 53rd Oscars.

03-31.title: Christopher Walken
03-31.description: Hypnotic character actor whose Oscar-winning turn in The Deer Hunter and unforgettable roles in Pulp Fiction and Batman Returns made him one of cinema's most singular presences.

03-31.title: Ewan McGregor
03-31.description: Scottish actor whose chameleonic energy lit up Trainspotting, Moulin Rouge, and the Star Wars prequels before a magisterial Obi-Wan Kenobi series closed the circle.

03-31.title: Herb Alpert
03-31.description: Trumpeter and co-founder of A&M Records whose Tijuana Brass made him one of the best-selling instrumental artists of the 1960s — and one of music's greatest business minds.

03-31.title: Eiffel Tower Inaugurated
03-31.description: Gustave Eiffel's iron lattice tower was officially opened for the Paris World's Fair — initially derided as an eyesore, it became the most visited monument on Earth.

03-31.title: Jimi Hendrix Burns His Guitar
03-31.description: At the Astoria Theatre in London, Jimi Hendrix set fire to his guitar onstage for the first time — a theatrical act of rock and roll sacrifice that became legend.

03-31.title: RCA Victor Unveils the 45 RPM Single
03-31.description: RCA Victor introduced the 7-inch 45 RPM vinyl single, a format that would become the currency of pop music and help birth rock and roll in the following decade.

03-31.title: The Sting
03-31.description: Paul Newman and Robert Redford's con-artist caper won seven Oscars including Best Picture at the 46th Academy Awards, making it the most lauded entertainment of its year.
